samples.summary: "neuters every write path" makes unasserted calls: setLocalSelection and recordSelectionForHistory leaking through would not fail the test
samples.evidence: In `it('neuters every write path')` the only assertions are `store.getText() === 'hello'` and `store.canUndo() === false`. `view.setLocalSelection(1, 2)` and `view.recordSelectionForHistory(...)` are called with no observable assertion, and with `MemNoteStore` they *have* no observable effect: `setLocalSelection` only writes the private `currentSelection` (memory.ts:204-210) and `getPeerSelections()` always returns `[]` (memory.ts:212). So if `setLocalSelection` were classified as a reader/forwarded (or added to NOTE_STORE_READERS by mistake), every assertion in this test would still pass. That is exactly the path the wrapper's own comment calls out as a CRDT presence write (`read-only.ts`: "publishing a caret is a `doc.update` like any other"), and per this diff's own reasoning (board-view/slides-view/pdf-collab guards) a viewer-role presence publish is refused by the enforcing auth webhook and wedges the viewer's sync. A `vi.spyOn(store, 'setLocalSelection')` / `recordSelectionForHistory` assertion (not-called) would close it.

samples.summary: New read-only guard on the PDF presence publish (`onActivePageChange`) has no test, though a test file was added for the sibling initialRoot change
samples.evidence: `pdf-collab.tsx` now early-returns from `onActivePageChange` when `readOnly`. The new `tests/app/files/pdf-collab-provider.test.tsx` covers only `initialRoot` ({} vs {comments:{}}); the existing `tests/app/files/pdf-collab.test.tsx` only ever mounts `PdfCollabStateProvider` with `readOnly={false}` (line 71) and never exercises page-change presence. Grepped `packages/frontend` for `onActivePageChange`/`activePage` in tests — no coverage of the read-only branch, so re-introducing the publish (which per the code comment wedges a viewer's whole sync) would ship green.

samples.summary: Read-only presence guards added to board-view and slides-view have no test at all
samples.evidence: `board-view.tsx` (`if (readOnly) return;` inside `onSelectionChange`) and `slides-view.tsx` (`if (readOnlyMount) return;` inside `broadcast`) are new behavior guards whose failure, by the diff's own reasoning, wedges a viewer's sync on the first click. Grepping `packages/frontend` for `updatePresence` finds only `yorkie-slides-store.test.ts` and `yorkie-board-store.test.ts` (store-level, not the view guard), and there is no board-view/slides-view component test (glob `packages/frontend/**/*{board,slides}*view*test*` returns only `board-preview-viewport.test.ts`). Note these views are canvas-heavy and may be intentionally untested — flagging as a contained gap.

samples.summary: `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv` and the missing-secret (`undefined` injector) branch are untested
samples.evidence: Grepping the repo for `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv` finds only its definition and the three ops scripts; no spec imports it. Also untested: `yorkieServiceTokenInjector(undefined)` returning `undefined`, and the `YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN` env override. `auth.service.spec.ts` covers only `signYorkieServiceToken` and `yorkieServiceTokenInjector(secret)`. Failure mode is loud-ish (scripts attach anonymously and get 401), hence minor.

samples.summary: No test joins a *keyed* service token to `verifyYorkieToken`, so the scoping seam is only ever tested with the verifier stubbed out
samples.evidence: `auth.service.spec.ts` round-trips only unkeyed service tokens (`signYorkieServiceToken('access-secret','10m')`) and asserts `typ`. `yorkie-auth.controller.spec.ts` supplies `{ typ:'yorkie-service', key:'sheet-1' }` via a stubbed `verifyYorkieToken`, and `yorkie.service.spec.ts` verifies the key with a bare `new JwtService().verify`. So nothing asserts that `AuthService.verifyYorkieToken` returns the `key` — if it were dropped/normalized away, `decideService` would see `!identity.key` and fall through to the blanket `ALLOW` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:289), silently converting every request-path token into a deployment-wide credential, with the whole suite green.

samples.summary: The divider resize changes (25px hit area, `touch-action: none`, ratio measured against `rect.width - divider.offsetWidth`) have no test
samples.evidence: Grepped `packages/notes` test files for `divider`, `splitRatio`, `touchAction`, `note-divider` — no matches; repo-wide `note-divider` appears only in `packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts`. The new `track` denominator changes the drag mapping (a user-visible pointer/pane offset) and the `touch-action` fix enables touch resizing at all; both would regress undetected. jsdom cannot lay out, so a test would have to stub `offsetWidth`/`getBoundingClientRect` — hence minor.

samples.summary: The uploader test asserts only the mocked factory's return, so it cannot detect a wrong/absent share-token wiring beyond prop identity
samples.evidence: `vi.mock('@/app/docs/image-insert', ...)` replaces `shareTokenImageUploader` with `(token) => async () => \`uploaded:${token}\``, and the test asserts `resolves.toBe('uploaded:tok-1')`. That confirms the token is threaded and the prop is a function, but the real uploader (endpoint, headers, 401 behaviour the comment in `shared-notes-layout.tsx` motivates) is mocked away, so this test is a wiring check only. Also `NotesView` itself is fully stubbed, so `viewMode`/`readOnly`/`uploadImage` assertions verify props, not view behaviour. Acceptable as a seam test; noting the limit.

samples.summary: `canUndo()/canRedo()` assertions in the read-only mount test hold for a fresh store regardless of the read-only gating
samples.evidence: `expect(api.canUndo()).toBe(false)` / `canRedo()` are asserted on a store built as `new MemNoteStore('hello')` with no prior edits, so both are false even without the new `!readOnly && ...` guard in `editor.ts`. The meaningful assertions in that test (`editText`/`undo` spies not called, text unchanged) do carry weight; only these two lines are non-discriminating. Pinning them would need an edit recorded on the store first.

verdict.reason: Verified as described. In read-only.test.ts:32-47 ('neuters every write path') the only assertions are undo()/redo() returning null, store.getText()==='hello', and store.canUndo()===false. view.recordSelectionForHistory (line 39) and view.setLocalSelection(1,2) (line 41) are called with no observable assertion, and with MemNoteStore they have no observable effect: setLocalSelection writes only the private currentSelection (memory.ts:204-210), getPeerSelections always returns [] (memory.ts:212-214), recordSelectionForHistory sets only private batchAfterSelection/currentSelection (memory.ts:167-171), and the batch pushes no undo unit because its neutered editText leaves text unchanged (memory.ts:149). currentSelection is surfaced only via undo/redo return values, and the undo stack is empty. So reclassifying setLocalSelection or recordSelectionForHistory into NOTE_STORE_READERS (read-only.ts:19-27, bound-forwarded at read-only.ts:123-124) would keep this test fully green, even though read-only.ts:138-143 documents the caret publish as a deliberate CRDT write that must be neutered. I grepped every *.test.* file for setLocalSelection and for readOnlyNoteStore: read-only.test.ts is the only test of the proxy, and no other test pins the presence write path, so no guard elsewhere makes the gap unreachable. A vi.spyOn not-called assertion would close it. Real, in-lane (unasserted calls presented as coverage under a test named 'every write path'), and blocking as a silently weakenable guard on the diff's central new behavior.
